provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
Rule: each marker cell (original colour 9) sits just outside one 3x3 square and has exactly one 4-neighbour that belongs to that square. Call the direction from the marker to that neighbour d.

- If the square is the absorbing colour (original 6), the marker is erased and a marker is painted at marker + 2d. This puts it on the square's middle row or column.
- If the square is the dissolving colour (original 5), the marker stays and the touched square cell also becomes a marker.
- Afterwards, every remaining dissolving-colour cell becomes background.

The rule treats all four orthogonal directions the same way, and it is defined by local adjacency. So any D4 transform keeps the same mechanism in visible coordinates: vertical inward moves become horizontal inward moves, and reflections reverse d automatically because d is read from the visible grid. No axis needs to be specialised.

The colour roles become the constants palette[8], palette[5], palette[6] and palette[9]. The emitted program works directly on the visible query grid. It does not normalise, invert, or permute colours.

The archived solver erases all marker sources first and then writes destinations. This ordering is kept, so a move that lands where another marker used to be cannot be overwritten. In the generator's domain this cannot happen anyway, because destinations are always inside squares and sources are always outside.
draft_notes.limitations:
- Domain assumptions from the generator: every marker is orthogonally adjacent to exactly one square cell; squares are separated by at least one cell; and moved or extended markers never collide (the generator rejects collisions).
- If a malformed input put a marker next to two different squares, the program would take the first neighbour in up/down/left/right order. That order is only a fallback, not part of the puzzle rule.
- Markers with no adjacent square are left unchanged; the generator never produces them.
- Demonstrations are not used, because the colour roles are fixed through the palette.
- I found no fixture contradictions or constructor indexing defects. The generator's clobber checks and its single-neighbour check (8-neighbourhood) remove ambiguous scenes.
- I have not run this code. The host's fixture checks and fresh-pair runs will be its first test.
draft_notes.host_review: Every side marker is adjacent to a unique block in the original eight-neighbour check; thus the solver four-neighbour inward direction is unique. Absorb6 moves two steps inward; dissolve5 retains source plus one step and clears block. New episode gate requires demonstration evidence for each queried colour/action role. Fixtures unchanged.
draft_notes.host_sampler_revision: Bounded packing preserves requested1..3 blocks on9/11 grids and2..7 on13/15. Enumerate legal side marker positions and draw1..5 with distinct output destinations. Retain marker multiplicity range, both block colours and all sides; reject a layout if requested markers cannot fit rather than lowering the count. Original draw still verifies every pair.
